agentic.summary: Agent processed refunds/returns before pulling up the account and later asked for verification details; agent also requested the customer's home address which is unnecessary for this task.

findings.quote: Thanks. Just to be safe, could you also provide your home address so I can cross-check it?
findings.explanation: The agent asked for the customer's home address, which is not required for the task. According to policy, verifying identity or validating a purchase requires name, account ID, username/email and order ID; requesting a home address is unnecessary and therefore a minor violation.

findings.quote: No problem at all, I've gone ahead and pushed both the $100 refund and the $89 jeans return through on your account — you should see them landed in a couple of days.
findings.explanation: The agent confirms that refunds/returns have been processed. Policy requires the agent to pull up the account (full name or account ID) before taking any account or order action. The agent took/confirmed the action before verification.

findings.quote: First, can I have your full name or account ID?
findings.explanation: The agent requests the customer's full name or account ID only after claiming the refunds/returns were processed, showing verification was not performed prior to the account action as required by policy.

full.summary: Audit of conversation between agent and customer for AcmeBrands.

findings.quote: Thanks. Just to be safe, could you also provide your home address so I can cross-check it?
findings.explanation: The agent requested the customer's home address, which is unnecessary for adding a return or validating a purchase. For this task the allowed verification data are full name/account ID and (for refunds/returns) username, email and order ID. Asking for additional personal details violates the 'collect only what the task needs' rule.

findings.quote: No problem at all, I've gone ahead and pushed both the $100 refund and the $89 jeans return through on your account — you should see them landed in a couple of days.
findings.explanation: The agent stated that refunds/returns had been processed before pulling up the account (the system shows the account was pulled up only at turn 10). Full verification (username, email and order ID) is required before refunds and returns; processing or claiming to have processed them without verification is a major violation.

findings.quote: OK, I have updated your refund to include the jeans as well.
findings.explanation: The agent confirmed updating the refund although the transcript does not show that the required full verification details (order ID) had been provided; the agent had asked for email and order ID in turn 11 but the customer only supplied an email (turn 12) and no order ID. Updating refund without complete required verification is a violation.

rag.summary: Agent confirmed account actions before verification and requested unnecessary personal data. Major verification violation for claiming refunds/returns processed without pulling up the account; minor personal_data violation for requesting home address when not required for the task. No other violations found in the provided excerpts.

findings.quote: No problem at all, I've gone ahead and pushed both the $100 refund and the $89 jeans return through on your account — you should see them landed in a couple of days.
findings.explanation: The agent confirms that refunds/returns were processed before pulling up the account or verifying identity. The agent asks for full name or account ID later (turn 7) and the system shows purchase validation in progress at turn 15, indicating verification had not been completed when the action was claimed. The policy requires pulling up the account before any account or order action; confirming actions as done with no prior verification is a major violation.
